name: Emelie Heintz
reason: The exact-name Stockholm health-economics profile is strongly aligned with EQ-5D research: it includes EQ-5D-3L/5L validity, QALY weights, and health-technology evaluation. The broad Swedish clinical portfolio is coherent with outcomes and cost-effectiveness work.

name: Emily McDool
reason: Exact-name University of Sheffield profile directly matches all listed EQ-HWB and EQ-5D work: it includes EQ-HWB-S valuation and psychometric studies, the EQ-HWB-9 population validity study, and repeated collaboration with Mukuria, Rowen, Brazier, and Carlton.

name: Eri Hoshino
reason: Although the record includes recent preference-measure and caregiver quality-of-life work, it contains substantial incompatible material spanning inorganic air-sample chemistry, veterinary VDR pharmacology, renal biology, salivary-gland oncology, and cardiothoracic surgery. This supports name-collision contamination, so it is unsafe to assign to the EQ-5D-Y valuation researcher.

name: Erica Lubetkin
reason: Erica I. Lubetkin's exact-name CUNY profile is a long, coherent EQ-5D and population health-related quality-of-life record. It includes EQ-5D US-population analyses and mapping, current EQ-DAPHNIE papers, and recurring EuroQol collaborators Janssen, Haagsma, and Bonsel.

name: Ernest Law
reason: Ernest H. Law's exact-name Pfizer profile is a coherent pharmaceutical outcomes portfolio spanning oncology and dermatology, with direct EuroQol evidence including US EQ-5D-5L valuation and parallel EQ-5D-3L/5L valuation. The isolated 1917 record is an obvious minor outlier, not substantial contamination.
